name: Commander Severin Bale
age: Not stated on the card — no birth year or age line the way some cards carry one (contrast Lord Knight Commander Maud Thole's card, which states '44' outright; Severin's Identity/Soul Architecture/Primary Stats sections give none). Cast as a seasoned veteran rather than a rookie: he is Head Captain over all Slayer cells across the Plateau theatres and personally trains regional Slayers, Dell among them (card, Duties: 'Train regional Slayers — Dell among them — and set thresholds for when not to swing'), which reads as a long career and an established mentor, plausibly mid-40s to mid-50s. Director's inference, not a sourced fact.
body: No height/build line on the card either. Inferred from mechanism: Anvil Step reads 'feet bite ground; recoil disappears into the floor, not his frame' (Traits) — a body built to ground massive recoil rather than dodge it — and his Dexterity (344, Grade A) trails well behind an Ardency sitting at the literal stat ceiling (542 of 550, Grade S), with the card itself noting he is 'Built for straight fights.' He also wields a two-handed slab-edge greatblade (Gallowsgate) with a coffin guard as an unremarkable extension of himself. Reads as large, dense, low-center-of-gravity — built like a foundation stone for delivering and absorbing force in a straight line, not a duelist's taper.
texture: faint ground-in grit from the role, not a growl
energy: Banked and heavy rather than explosive. The kit's whole logic is control, not fury: latches that trap a weapon instead of trading blows with it, a coffin guard that turns aside a charge by planting rather than parrying, a gauntlet that silences a single breath instead of brawling a spell down. He does not need volume — the card's own magic says his calm is load-bearing: once he 'points the blade and declares a name, everything that protects that life grows heavy' (Traits, Sentence Weight), and a spoken order carries 'execution priority' — panic itself forgets how to scatter when he says stand (Traits, Black Writ). Play the menace as certainty, never as rising heat.
register: Procedural, writ-and-oath language — Black Watch officialese delivered flat: name the target, state the sentence, close the book. No persuasion register and no negotiation; per Relationships, the Reaper ratifies and adjudicates while 'the Slayer executes and cannot adjudicate' — he is not building a case, he is reading a warrant that is already final.

reference_direction: Male, very low pitch with heavy chest resonance, dry/dense texture and only faint ground-in grit — no growl, no rasp for effect. Pace is unhurried to the point of stillness ('I don't hurry'), each clause set down and left there rather than rushed into the next. No regional or ethnic accent is assigned to him anywhere in the corpus — play it plain and institutional, a Black Watch officer's voice, not a folk voice. Closest comparison: a hanging judge reading a warrant aloud in a quiet room — the sentence is already decided before the first word is spoken, so nothing in the delivery needs to argue for it.
